notes:
Account summary
- Northpeak Research is an AI startup building a developer-facing research assistant (RAG + summarization + light tool use). Considering Redwood Hosted API for production and evaluating Dedicated later if throughput increases.

What they care about (verbatim / paraphrase)
- “We need an RSS or JSON feed of model updates. Otherwise we can’t operationalize change-management.”
- “If we pin a model version, we need to see the resolved version in the API response and a link to what changed.”
- Wants compatibility notes per version: context length changes, tool/function calling support, structured output guarantees, embeddings dimensionality (if applicable), deprecation timeline + replacement model.

Current setup / context
- They’re integrating with an OpenAI-compatible client today; prefer minimal client changes.
- They monitor latency/cost tightly; open to using Redwood Optimize guidance, but first priority is transparency + predictability.

Key requirements (from demo)
- Machine-readable changelog:
  - JSON feed endpoint with pagination + filters by model_id/date; ETag support so they can poll efficiently.
  - RSS/Atom feed is a nice-to-have, but they will accept JSON as long as it’s stable and documented.
- API/SDK surfaces:
  - Response includes resolved model_version and a changelog_url.
  - Clear statement of compatibility guarantees when pinning model versions (no silent upgrades).
- Release notes content:
  - Needs “impact” + “compatibility” sections even for small changes.
  - Wants deprecation fields with dates and replacement model where available.

Risks / concerns
- Past experience with other vendors: model behavior changed without notice; they’re explicitly trying to avoid outages/regressions during customer trials.
- They asked whether Redwood will ever change weights/config under the same version identifier (answer: should be no; any change requires new version_id + changelog entry).

Internal actions
- SE (Quentin) to share early draft of customer-visible changelog format and how it will show up in Console + docs site.
- Owner (Dylan) to confirm timeline for exposing changelog feed + headers for OpenAI-compatible endpoints; customer asked for beta access when ready.

Next steps
- Send follow-up with: (1) planned JSON feed shape + caching semantics, (2) example changelog entry showing compatibility notes, (3) how pinned version + rollback works, (4) proposed beta timeline + feedback loop.
